error.signature: AI tells someone in South Korea to call 1393 for suicide-prevention counseling, or implies Korea's mental-health crisis line can never involve outside intervention

verdict.summary: South Korea's 1393 (자살예방상담전화) suicide-prevention line was retired and consolidated, along with several other counseling lines across 8 agencies, into a single unified number, 109, effective January 1, 2024, per the Ministry of Health and Welfare (MOHW). 109 is free, 24/7, and run via the 129 Comprehensive Counseling Center; counseling content is fundamentally confidential, but if a caller is assessed to be in imminent danger, the counselor can request help from other agencies - MOHW describes 109 as coordinating with 112 emergency dispatch for high-risk cases, not as a replacement for it.

dead_ends.action: Tell someone in South Korea to call 1393 for suicide-prevention or mental-health crisis counseling
dead_ends.why_fails: 1393 was retired and consolidated, along with several other counseling lines across 8 agencies, into a single unified number, 109, effective January 1, 2024, per the Ministry of Health and Welfare. An AI citing 1393 after that date is giving a dead number.
dead_ends.common_misconception: 1393 is still widely cited in older articles, forum posts, and outdated guides, so models trained on that material default to it.

dead_ends.action: Assume Korea's 109 mental-health counseling line is fully confidential with no possibility of outside intervention, the same as a purely anonymous peer-support line
dead_ends.why_fails: The official 109 program page states that while counseling content is fundamentally confidential ('상담 내용은 기본적으로 비밀이 보장됩니다'), if the caller is assessed to be in critical/imminent danger, the counselor can request help from other agencies ('상담 대상자가 위급한 경우 다른 기관 등으로 도움을 요청할 수 있습니다') - MOHW describes 109 as coordinating with 112 emergency dispatch for high-risk cases, not as a replacement for it.
dead_ends.condition: Caller assessed as high imminent risk

dead_ends.action: Tell someone that Korea's older mental-health line, 1577-0199, was merged into 109 along with 1393
dead_ends.why_fails: MOHW's January 2024 consolidation folded 1393 and several other counseling lines into 109, but 1577-0199 continues to operate separately - conflating the two can send someone to the wrong line.
dead_ends.condition: Distinguishing 109 from other Korean mental-health numbers

workarounds.action: For mental-health crisis counseling in South Korea (current as of 2024 onward), call 109 - free, 24/7, run by the Ministry of Health and Welfare via the 129 Comprehensive Counseling Center.

Be aware that if a 109 counselor assesses imminent danger to life during a call, 109 can coordinate with 112 emergency dispatch - treat 109 as capable of escalating to physical intervention when necessary, not purely anonymous peer support.
For an active emergency requiring immediate police or ambulance response, call 112 (police) or 119 (fire/ambulance) directly rather than only 109.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: 112/119 are direct emergency dispatch numbers; 109 is primarily counseling-first, with dispatch-capable escalation only when a counselor assesses imminent risk.
